info.title: speed
info.description: The platform API: every operation the assembled modules declare, merged from the OpenAPI fragment each module generates from its own operation declarations. Each operation is tagged with the module that declared it, and each names the security requirement its route admits.

get.description: Handles a provider's callback as a top-level browser navigation. The callback is bound through the flow cookie only, because a navigation cannot set a request header; the path's provider must equal the provider recorded in the flow and the flow must be at its first factor, otherwise the call is a 401 flow-invalid before any method is asked. The engine moves the flow to processing before calling the method, so a replayed authorization code or assertion loses the compare-and-swap and gets 401 flow-invalid. A GET callback that carries no flow cookie is always 401 flow-invalid: an identity-provider-initiated sign-in is served only as a POST. A cookie login that completes on this route answers 303 to the flow's stored return target instead of a body. A token-delivery login whose request declares a navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`) answers 303 the same way, with no session made and the flow left at ready; without that declaration it is answered the completion body. A callback of a purpose other than login (a link, or a step-up of an account with no factor) that reaches ready answers 303 the same way, with no session made: the flow stays in the cookie at ready for the host's callback page to read with `GET /auth/flows/current` and complete with `POST /auth/flows/answer`.

parameters.description: The provider this callback is for: a social method's stable name, or, for an enterprise SSO provider, the identifier the start named in `input.provider`. It must equal the provider recorded in the flow the callback is bound to; a mismatch is a 401 flow-invalid and the callback never reaches a method.
parameters.name: provider

200.description: The flow, advanced by the callback, as answered to an API callback: a token-delivery login whose callback declares no navigation. A login that declares a navigation is answered 303 instead.

When the flow recorded no return target, the configured `authn.login.default-return-to` is used.

post.description: Handles a provider's callback delivered as a cross-site form post, which is how SAML's assertion consumer service is reached. The callback is bound through the flow cookie only, because a form post cannot set a request header; the path's provider must equal the provider recorded in the flow and the flow must be at its first factor, otherwise the call is a 401 flow-invalid before any method is asked. The posted form is bounded to 512 KiB before it is parsed, and a body over that bound is answered 401 login-failed with the flow left a tombstone. The engine moves the flow to processing before calling the method, so an assertion is handled at most once. A token-delivery login whose request declares a navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`) answers 303 to the flow's stored return target with no session made and the flow left at ready; without that declaration it is answered the completion body. A callback of a purpose other than login (a link, or a step-up of an account with no factor) that reaches ready answers 303 to the flow's stored return target, with no session made and the flow left in the cookie for the host's callback page to read with `GET /auth/flows/current` and complete with `POST /auth/flows/answer`. Without a flow cookie the route serves an identity-provider-initiated sign-in, but only for an enterprise provider whose row enables it.

parameters.description: The provider this callback is for: a social method's stable name, or, for an enterprise SSO provider, the identifier the start named in `input.provider`. It must equal the provider recorded in the flow the callback is bound to; a mismatch is a 401 flow-invalid and the callback never reaches a method.

get.description: Answers every factor row the caller's account has registered, ordered oldest first by creation time and then by identifier. Each row carries the kind, label, lifecycle status and the instants it was created, activated and last used; it carries no seed, key, public key or other data a kind keeps for itself. The list is empty when the account has registered none.

200.description: The caller's factors, without any seed, key or other secret of a kind's own

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

503.description: The factors could not be listed: the factor store was unavailable. The cause is logged and not sent

get.summary: List the caller's own registered factors

delete.description: Removes one factor of the caller's account: whatever the factor's kind keeps for it is removed, then its register row. After an active factor has been removed, the account's other sessions are ended first and the session that made the request is then rotated: the 204 carries that session's new cookie, and the token the request was made with no longer authenticates. A pending or disabled factor ends no session and rotates none, and a session store that fails after the factor is gone is reported as an outage. The call requires a fresh multi-factor authentication verified locally, so one merely declared by an identity provider does not satisfy it; the requirement is the effective account's and the proof is the caller's own, so an impersonating identity removes the impersonated account's factor. A factor that is not the caller's answers the same as one already gone, so the route never answers 404 and repeating a removal is idempotent: it finishes any session revocation and rotation an earlier attempt could not. When the account has mfa_required set, its last active factor cannot be removed.

parameters.description: The factor identifier, as returned in `id` by `GET /auth/factors`. Empty or longer than 64 bytes is refused as a bad request without reading the register.
parameters.name: id

204.description: The factor was removed, or is not the caller's and reads as already gone; repeating a removal is idempotent. When an active factor was removed, the answer also sets the requesting session's new cookie, and the token the request was made with no longer authenticates

400.description: The factor identifier is malformed

401.description: No usable credential, or a fresh multi-factor authentication is required

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge. An unusable credential is challenged with the Bearer and Cookie schemes; a fresher authentication is challenged with the scheme the identity authenticated with, the level it must reach and, when one applies, a maximum age.

409.description: The factor is the account's last active factor, which cannot be removed while the account requires multi-factor authentication

503.description: The removal could not be completed: the factor store, the account data it needs or the session store was unavailable. The cause is logged and not sent. When the factor itself was already removed, repeating the request finishes ending the other sessions and rotating the requesting session

delete.summary: Remove one of the caller's own factors

patch.description: Writes the display label of one factor of the caller's account and answers the updated row, as `GET /auth/factors` shows it. The label is metadata, so the call asks for no freshness beyond the login session itself, and an impersonating identity renames the impersonated account's factor. The value is trimmed of surrounding whitespace and must be at most 64 characters with no control character; an empty value clears the name, and the module generates none. A factor that is not the caller's answers 404 with the problem type urn:speed:authn:factor-not-found, the same as one that is not there, so another account's identifier says nothing about whether it exists.

parameters.description: The factor identifier, as returned in `id` by `GET /auth/factors`. Empty or longer than 64 bytes is refused as a bad request without reading the register.
parameters.name: id

schema.description: The new display label of one factor the caller's account registered.

label.description: The factor's new display label: at most 64 characters with no control character. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before it is stored, and an empty value clears the name; the module generates none.

requestBody.description: The factor's new label. The member is required and an empty value clears the name; surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and at most 64 characters with no control character is stored. An unknown member is refused.

200.description: The factor row as it reads after the rename

400.description: The factor identifier is malformed, or the label is outside its domain

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

404.description: No factor of the caller's account has this identifier: it is not there, or it belongs to another account. Both cases answer the problem type urn:speed:authn:factor-not-found

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

503.description: The factor could not be renamed: the factor store was unavailable. The cause is logged and not sent

post.description: Starts a login flow for the method named in the body and advances it through the method's first step. The flow token is written to the flow cookie, or, with `binding` set to `header`, returned in `flow_token` with no cookie; later calls are bound to the flow by that token. The route reads no cookie, so a stale session cookie does not prevent a login. Depending on the method and the multi-factor policy, the returned flow may already stand at a second-factor, enrollment or ready step. A body that is not `application/json` is a 415, an unknown member or a value outside its domain is a 400, and a credential the method did not accept is a 401 login-failed — except two refusals the route answers as a 400: a phone prefix the deployment does not allow (`unsupported-region`) and an identifier that cannot name an account (`bad-request`). A 429 carries `Retry-After` when the back-off states a delay.

schema.description: The start request; `method` must name a login method this deployment takes in, or the call is a bad request.

binding.description: How the flow token is carried: `cookie` (the default) writes the flow cookie (`__Host-authn-flow`) and returns no token in the body; `header` returns the token in `flow_token` and sets no cookie, so the client must send it in the `Authn-Flow` request header on every later call. A callback navigation cannot set a header, so a flow bound this way cannot finish a redirect method.

delivery.description: How a completed login is delivered: `session` (the default) sets the session cookie and answers the session view; `token` answers an access and refresh token pair. `token` must be enabled by the deployment and requires the token capability, otherwise the request is a 400 bad-request.

human_proof.description: The human-verification proof the deployment may require before it sends a verification message: a Turnstile token, a captcha answer or a proof-of-work token. It is ignored when the deployment requires none. A value longer than 8 KiB is a 400 bad-request before any provider is asked; a missing or invalid proof is a 403 human-verification-required and no message is sent.

input.description: The fields the method's first step takes, as name-to-value strings. At most 8 members, each value at most 512 bytes; anything beyond is a 400 bad-request.

method.description: The stable name of a login method, as returned in `name` by `GET /auth/methods`. A name the deployment does not take in is a 400 bad-request; a method turned off by the deployment is a 403 method-disabled.

purpose.description: Accepted but not read by this route: a flow started here always has the purpose login. Use `POST /auth/flows/authenticated` for link, step-up or enroll.

return_to.description: Where the callback lands the user agent: either a path starting with a single `/`, not `//`, without backslash, control characters or `@` and at most 2048 bytes, or an absolute URL whose origin the deployment trusts; anything else is a 400 bad-request. The callback lands the user agent there for every purpose that reaches ready: a login, a link and a no-factor step-up. An absent or empty value uses the configured `authn.login.default-return-to`, which is held to the same rule and falls back to `/`. The value is stored in the flow record, and no parameter of the callback request can change it.

requestBody.description: The start request: the method to run, how the flow token is carried, where to return after a completed login, and the fields the method's first step takes. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

200.description: The flow, advanced to its first step

400.description: The body could not be read, a value is outside its domain, or the method refused the identifier as a region the deployment does not serve (`unsupported-region`) or as one that cannot name an account (`bad-request`)

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

post.description: Advances the flow the request is bound to by one step. The body must echo the flow's current `seq`, or the call is a 401 flow-invalid. A refused answer is not progress: it keeps the step and its `seq`, counting only against the eight-answer limit, so the same `seq` answers again once the value is corrected. `step` must be one of `answer`, `factor`, `enroll` or `complete`: a name outside that set is a 400 bad-request, and a step the flow's state does not accept is a 401 flow-invalid. A flow accepts at most eight client answers, after which it is moved to failed and every later answer is a 401 flow-invalid. The answer is the flow at its next step or, once the flow is ready, the completed result: the session view, the token pair, or the `linked`/`enrolled` result of a link or enrollment. Each step is a compare-and-swap on the flow record, so concurrent answers are decided by the store and the loser gets 401 flow-invalid rather than a retry.

schema.description: One answer to the bound flow: which step is being answered, the step number to echo, and the fields the step takes.

human_proof.description: The human-verification proof the deployment may require before it sends a verification message: a Turnstile token, a captcha answer or a proof-of-work token. It is ignored when the deployment requires none. A value longer than 8 KiB is a 400 bad-request before any provider is asked; a missing or invalid proof is a 403 human-verification-required and no message is sent.

input.description: The fields the step takes, as name-to-value strings. At most 8 members, each value at most 8 KiB; a second-factor step reads `factor` to choose the factor and then the values that factor asks for, an enrollment step reads `kind`, and `complete` reads nothing.

seq.description: The `seq` of the flow as last returned. It must equal the record's current step number; a stale or future value is a 401 flow-invalid.

step.description: The step being answered: `answer` for a first-factor submission, only while the flow is at the first factor; `factor` for a second-factor step, only at the second factor; `enroll` for an enrollment step, only at the enroll state; `complete` to take the result of a ready flow. A name outside this set is a 400 bad-request, and a step that does not match the flow's state is a 401 flow-invalid.

requestBody.description: One answer to the bound flow: the step number to echo, the step being answered, and the fields that step takes. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

200.description: The flow advanced, or completed with a session or a token pair

400.description: The username a pending first login would open the account with does not normalize

401.description: The credential did not hold, or the flow binding is missing or wrong

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The account is unavailable, or an SMS second-factor challenge or enrollment is refused because the account has no proved phone (phone-required), or a human-verification proof is missing or invalid (human-verification-required)

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state: a completed link names an external identity another account already holds, or the username a pending first login would open the account with is already taken (username-taken). A step that does not match the flow's state is a 401 flow-invalid, not a 409.

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

post.description: Starts a `link`, `step-up` or `enroll` flow on the identity the gateway authenticated and advances it to its first step. The flow is bound to the effective account and the caller's session: an impersonating identity starts it for the impersonated account and proves its own factors. A link and an enrollment require the fresh authentication the effective account's factors call for — a fresh local multi-factor when the account holds an active factor, a fresh first factor otherwise — and answer 401 insufficient_user_authentication with `WWW-Authenticate` when it does not hold. A step-up whose account holds at least one factor usable for this session starts at the second factor and answers the offered factors without calling the method. An account whose factors were all activated at or after the session authenticated starts at a first factor the body names, or at its password when the body names none or names one this deployment does not take in, and offers those factors as the second step; naming a password the account cannot prove is a 400 bad-request, and an account with no first factor to prove again is refused with 401 insufficient_user_authentication. An account with no factor starts at the first factor the body names. The delivery mode is not read from the body: it follows the kind of the request's session.

schema.description: The start request for a purpose other than login; `purpose` must be `link`, `step-up` or `enroll`.

binding.description: How the flow token is carried: `cookie` (the default) writes the flow cookie (`__Host-authn-flow`) and returns no token in the body; `header` returns the token in `flow_token` and sets no cookie, so the client must send it in the `Authn-Flow` request header on every later call. A callback navigation cannot set a header, so a flow bound this way cannot finish a redirect method.

delivery.description: Accepted but not read: the delivery mode follows the kind of the request's session. It is accepted so that a client may send this route the same start body it sends to `POST /auth/flows`.

human_proof.description: The human-verification proof the deployment may require before it sends a verification message: a Turnstile token, a captcha answer or a proof-of-work token. It is ignored when the deployment requires none. A value longer than 8 KiB is a 400 bad-request before any provider is asked; a missing or invalid proof is a 403 human-verification-required and no message is sent.

input.description: The fields the started step takes, as name-to-value strings: the method's first step for `link` and for a step-up that starts at the first factor, the enrollment step for `enroll` where `kind` names the factor kind and an optional `label` names the factor (at most 64 characters after trimming surrounding whitespace, without control characters; a value outside that domain is a 400 bad-request), except that a kind an account may hold only once -- the authenticator app -- takes no name, and a label sent for it is that same 400 bad-request, and nothing for a step-up that starts at the second factor, except that a step-up may also name `exclude_factor`, one factor the flow must not offer -- the factor the caller is about to delete, which must never prove its own removal; a value naming no factor of the account filters nothing. When that exclusion leaves the account no factor at all, the flow of an account holding a password starts at the password and completes on it alone, while an account without a password is refused with 401 `insufficient_user_authentication`. At most 8 members, each value at most 512 bytes.

method.description: The method to run for `link` and for a `step-up` of an account that holds no factor. For an enrollment it is not read. A step-up starts at the second factor when the session may use a factor the account registered before it authenticated. When every factor was registered during this session, the flow starts at the first factor this names, or at the password when it names none or names one the deployment does not take in, and offers those factors as the second step. Naming `password` there for an account that cannot prove one is a 400 bad-request, as is any name the deployment does not take in for a step-up of an account that holds no factor; an account with no password and no named method is refused with 401 insufficient_user_authentication.

purpose.description: Required, and one of `link`, `step-up` or `enroll`: bind an external identity, strengthen the current session, or register a factor. Any other value, including an empty one, is a 400 bad-request.

return_to.description: Where the callback lands the user agent: either a path starting with a single `/`, not `//`, without backslash, control characters or `@` and at most 2048 bytes, or an absolute URL whose origin the deployment trusts; anything else is a 400 bad-request. The callback lands the user agent there for every purpose that reaches ready: a login, a link and a no-factor step-up. An absent or empty value uses the configured `authn.login.default-return-to`, which is held to the same rule and falls back to `/`. The value is stored in the flow record, and no parameter of the callback request can change it.

requestBody.description: The request to start a link, step-up or enrollment flow: the purpose, the method and fields where the purpose takes them, how the flow token is carried, and the return target. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

get.description: Reads the flow the request is bound to so a client can resume it, for example after a page refresh or after a callback sent the user agent back. The flow token is taken from the flow cookie or the `Authn-Flow` header, and a flow bound by the header gets it echoed in `flow_token`. A missing or mismatched binding, and a flow that is done, failed or gone, are all answered 401 flow-invalid. The reply is built from the stored record alone, so a first-factor step the method named cannot be re-prompted with its fields and its `next.kind` is `challenge`.

post.description: Issues one human-verification challenge for the self-hosted captcha mechanism. Only the `audio` form may be chosen: the `form` query item naming it draws a spoken reading of digits as the screen-reader alternative. The `scope` query item names the surface the challenge is issued for: `phone` for a send that delivers a message to a phone number, `other` for every send that does not. It is required, and a missing or unknown value is a 400. The server rotates between the image and the slider form from a cryptographic random source, so `form=image`, `form=slider` and an absent item are all answered with whichever of the two the rotation drew; the value is not honoured, and any other value is a 400. The `lang` query item names the language an audio challenge is spoken in; the provider pronounces English, Japanese, Russian and Chinese, an unsupported language is a 400, and an absent item uses the request's active locale. The answer names the challenge id, the form, the instruction key a client words for that form, and the media paths the form carries. A proof is the challenge id and the answer joined by a dot; it is single-use, bound to the scope it was issued for, and spends the challenge whether the answer matched or not. A source that asks for more challenges than the window of the form it is requesting allows, or than the deployment-wide bound leaves for all sources together, is answered 429; the rotating forms keep a larger per-source bound, the audio form has its own stricter one, and the two counters neither spend nor are spent by the other. A key-value store that cannot answer is answered 503.

parameters.description: The surface the challenge is issued for: phone for a send that delivers a message to a phone number, other for every send that does not. Required; a missing or unknown value is a 400. A proof is bound to it: presenting it on the other surface is refused.
parameters.name: scope

parameters.description: The challenge form. Only audio is honoured: it draws the spoken reading of digits, the screen-reader alternative. The value image or slider, or an absent item, is ignored: the server rotates between those two forms from a cryptographic random source and answers whichever it drew. Any other value is a 400 bad-request.
parameters.name: form

parameters.description: The language the audio form's digits are spoken in, as a BCP 47 tag. The provider pronounces English, Japanese, Russian and Chinese; a tag naming another language is a 400. Absent or empty uses the request's active locale, falling back to English for a locale the provider does not pronounce. Ignored by the rotating forms.
parameters.name: lang

200.description: A captcha challenge, its form, its instruction key and its media paths

400.description: The scope item is missing or unknown, or the form or audio language is not one this provider draws

429.description: This source has asked for more challenges than the window of the form it is requesting allows, or all sources together have used up the deployment-wide bound; the audio form has its own, stricter per-source bound than the rotating forms. Retry later

503.description: The challenge could not be issued because the key-value store was unavailable

post.description: Issues one human-verification challenge for the proof-of-work mechanism. The `scope` query item names the surface the challenge is issued for: `phone` for a send that delivers a message to a phone number, `other` for every send that does not. It is required, and a missing or unknown value is a 400. The client solves the challenge by finding a nonce whose SHA-256 hash, over the decoded challenge followed by the nonce in big-endian, carries at least `difficulty` leading zero bits, then presents `challenge.nonce` as the proof to the send it wants to make. A proof is single-use and bound to the scope it was issued for: the challenge is spent when it is accepted, and presenting the proof on the other surface is refused. A source that asks for more challenges than its own window allows, or than the deployment-wide bound leaves for all sources together, is answered 429; a key-value store that cannot answer is answered 503.

parameters.description: The surface the challenge is issued for: phone for a send that delivers a message to a phone number, other for every send that does not. Required; a missing or unknown value is a 400. A proof is bound to it: presenting it on the other surface is refused.
parameters.name: scope

200.description: A challenge, its difficulty and its lifetime

400.description: The scope item is missing or names no surface this gate serves

429.description: This source has asked for more challenges than its own window allows, or all sources together have used up the deployment-wide bound; retry later
