verify_token.description: The token to publish in DNS

AuthnImpersonationGrant.description: An impersonation record as a client sees it. The reason and the administrator's identity are not part of it.

ends_at.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the record stops being valid; never more than one hour after it began.

id.description: Identifier of the impersonation record, minted when the start was granted.

started_at.description: Absent on the answer to a start, present on a record in force

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the impersonation is confined to

AuthnImpersonationGrantEnvelope.description: The answer of the status route.

grant.description: The record in force on the session, including the instant it began.

AuthnImpersonationStart.description: The answer of a start: the record just created and, for a bearer credential, the impersonation access token.

access_token.description: Present on a bearer start; absent on a cookie start, whose carrier is the session cookie

expires_in.description: Present with access_token; the access token's lifetime in whole seconds

grant.description: The record just created; started_at is absent because a start answer does not carry the start instant.

account.description: Identifier of the authenticated account the membership belongs to.

active.description: Whether the membership is active; a suspended membership is refused rather than reactivated.

source.description: The membership's source: invite when this acceptance created it, the source it already had when it was there.

sso_exempt.description: Whether the membership is exempt from SSO enforcement; an existing exemption is preserved.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the membership was written in.

AuthnInviteInvitation.description: One invitation as the management face shows it. It never carries the acceptance token.

accepted_at.description: The zero instant 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z when the invitation has not been accepted

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC of issuance.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 deadline in UTC; a pending invitation at or past it can no longer be accepted.

id.description: The invitation's opaque identifier, used to revoke it.

invited_by.description: The account identifier of the issuer; empty when a host command issued the invitation without an HTTP identity.

status.description: The stored state. Expiry is not stored: an expired pending invitation still reads pending.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the invitation grants a membership in.

AuthnInviteIssued.description: The answer of an issue: the invitation's view, the outcome of the notice, and the one-time acceptance token only when the notice did not reach the address.

email_delivery.description: How the acceptance notice ended: sent when the carrier accepted it, failed when delivery failed or its outcome is unknown, and not_configured when the assembly delivers no mail. A failed notice does not undo the invitation, and the token beside it is still the one-time link; a sent notice carries no token in this answer.

invitation.description: The issued invitation; a token is delivered beside it only when the notice did not reach the address.

token.description: The acceptance token, present only when email_delivery is failed or not_configured: the inviter has to hand the link over. Absent when the notice was sent, because the recipient already holds it.

AuthnInvitePage.description: One page of a tenant's invitations together with the cursor of the next page.

invitations.description: The invitations of this page, ordered by status ascending (pending, accepted, revoked) and then newest first with the identifier as the tie-break.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page, empty on the last page

AuthnInviteView.description: The answer of the acceptance read: the invitation's state, and its summary only while it can still be redeemed.

invitation.description: The invitation summary, present only for a pending invitation that can still be redeemed.

state.description: The state the read judges. Only pending carries the invitation summary: expired, accepted and revoked answer the state alone, without the invited address, the tenant's name or the deadline.

AuthnLoginActionResult.description: The answer of a flow that finished by binding an external identity (`linked`) or registering a factor (`enrolled`); neither issues a session or a token.

state.description: linked when the flow bound an external identity; enrolled when it registered a factor

AuthnLoginAnswer.description: One of four shapes, told apart by `state` and the members present: an open flow, a completed login delivered as a session, a completed login delivered as a token pair or an elevated step-up, or the result of a link or enrollment.

AuthnLoginFactor.description: One second factor the flow offers to verify: its identifier, its kind and a display label. It carries nothing secret.

id.description: The factor's identifier; send it as `input.factor` when answering the second-factor step.

kind.description: The factor kind, such as `totp`, `sms` or `webauthn`; the client renders the challenge according to it.

label.description: A display label for the factor; it may be empty, in which case the client falls back to the kind's own name.

AuthnLoginField.description: One input a method asks the client for, named by the method and rendered according to its kind.

kind.description: How the client renders the input: `text`, `password`, `code` or `phone`.

name.description: The input's key: the client submits its value under this name in the `input` map of the start request or of the answer.

required.description: Whether the step needs a value; absent means the field may be left out.

secret.description: Whether the value must not be displayed or echoed, as for a password or a code; absent means it is not secret.

AuthnLoginFlow.description: One open login flow, as returned by a start, by an answer that keeps the flow open, or by the current-flow read: the step number the next answer must echo, the flow's state, the flow token when the flow is bound by the header, and what the client does next.

flow_token.description: The flow token, set only when the flow is bound by the Authn-Flow header

next.description: What the client does at the flow's current step.

seq.description: The step number the next answer must echo

state.description: The flow's state: first, signup, second, enroll, reprove, ready, processing, done or failed

AuthnLoginHuman.description: The human-verification gate a deployment puts in front of every send of a verification message, reported once per surface. A deployment may run a different mechanism on each: the phone surface guards the four SMS sends, and the other surface guards every send that does not address a phone number. A deployment whose gate is off reports the off mechanism on both surfaces.

other.description: The gate on every send that does not address a phone number: an email reset code and a self-service email addition.

phone.description: The gate on a send that delivers a message to a phone number: login, second factor, enrollment and anonymous reset by SMS.

AuthnLoginHumanGate.description: The human-verification gate one surface runs: whether a proof is required, the mechanism that checks it, the public identifier a client-side widget needs, and the action that widget must be rendered with. A surface whose gate is off reports the off mechanism and requires nothing.

action.description: The action a client-side widget must be rendered with, for a mechanism that needs one; absent for `off`, `pow` and `captcha`. The provider's answer must name it.

provider.description: The mechanism that checks a proof on this surface: `off` when the gate is off, `pow` for the self-hosted proof of work, `captcha` for the self-hosted captcha, or `turnstile` for Cloudflare's widget

required.description: Whether every send on this surface must first present a valid, single-use proof

site_key.description: The public identifier a client-side widget is rendered with, for a mechanism that needs one; absent for `off`, `pow` and `captcha`

AuthnLoginIdentifierState.description: The answer of adding an identifier: `added` when the identifier is written, `pending` when a code was sent to an email address and the answer is still to come. The two durations are present only in the pending state.

expires_in.description: How long the code lives, in seconds; absent when the state is added

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in seconds; absent when the state is added

state.description: added when the identifier is written; pending when a code was sent to an address and its answer is still to come

AuthnLoginMFA.description: The second-factor kinds the deployment takes in, as the multi-factor module reports them. This is a deployment-level list, not the caller's own registered factors.

factors.description: The kinds of second factor the deployment takes in

AuthnLoginMethods.description: The discovery document of the login surface: one descriptor per login method that takes part and is not turned off, whether registration is open, the second-factor kinds the deployment takes in, and the human-verification gate this deployment requires before a verification message is sent. Enterprise identity providers are not listed here; they are discovered through the SSO module.

human.description: The human-verification gate a send must satisfy.

methods.description: The methods taking part that are not turned off, one descriptor each, sorted by name

mfa.description: The second-factor kinds the deployment takes in.

password_reset.description: Whether this deployment offers the anonymous password reset, and the channels it may use.

signup.description: Whether registration is open on this deployment: true when either `authn.account.signup` or `authn.account.password-signup` is `open`.

AuthnLoginPasswordReset.description: Whether this deployment offers the anonymous password reset and through which channels. It is a deployment fact, the same for every anonymous caller, and it says nothing about whether any account can be reset.

enabled.description: Whether the anonymous password reset is open: the switch is open, the audit record is present, and at least one channel is available

methods.description: The channels the reset may be sent through: email and sms, sorted, leaving out a channel that is not assembled, whose template is missing or that a disabled method turned off

AuthnLoginPasswordResetState.description: The state of the bound anonymous password reset: whether a code was sent or the identifier is proved, how long the code or the proved ticket lives, and, while a code is outstanding, how soon another may be asked for. It carries no account, no identifier and no code.

expires_in.description: How long the code or the proved ticket lives, in whole seconds

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in whole seconds; absent once the identifier is proved

state.description: sent after a code was sent, verified once the code held

AuthnLoginPhoneChallenge.description: The answer to a phone-verification send: how long the code lives and how soon another code may be asked for, both in whole seconds. It carries neither the challenge identifier nor any fact about whether the number is already held by another account.

expires_in.description: How long the code lives, in seconds

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in seconds

AuthnLoginRegistration.description: The answer of an anonymous self-registration: the state name `registered`, the account that was opened, and the email address awaiting verification. No session is made and no email is sent.

account_id.description: The identifier of the account that was opened

state.description: The literal `registered`, marking that an account was opened

AuthnLoginRegistrationContact.description: The contact a new registration has to prove: the pending state of the email address the caller gave, which is not yet a login name.

email.description: The email address the caller gave, awaiting verification

state.description: The verification state of the email address: `pending` until the address is proved after signing in

AuthnLoginSession.description: The answer of a login completed with `delivery=session`, and of a step-up completed on a cookie session: the state name `authenticated` and the public facts of the session that was created or elevated. The session cookie is set in the same response.

session.description: The public facts of the session the login created.

state.description: The literal `authenticated`, marking a completed login.

AuthnLoginSessionView.description: The public facts of the session a login created. No token or secret is included.

expires_at.description: The session's expiry as an RFC 3339 instant, or empty

id.description: The session identifier; the browser client holds the session cookie written in the same response.

AuthnLoginSignup.description: Whether anonymous self-registration is available on this deployment: either a first login may open an account, or the name-and-password register route is open. The two switches are independent; each member below reports its own.

enabled.description: Whether anonymous self-registration is available: true when either a first login may open an account or the name-and-password register route is open

password.description: Whether the name-and-password register route is open.

AuthnLoginSignupPassword.description: Whether the anonymous name-and-password register route is open, reported on its own because it is independent of a first login opening an account.

AuthnLoginStep.description: What the client does at the flow's current step. Only the members that belong to `kind` are present: `challenge` carries `fields`; a pending signup of a social first login also carries `provided_method`, `provided_display_name` and `provided_email`; `redirect` carries `url` and `method`; `factor` carries `factors`; `enroll` carries `kinds`; `webauthn` carries `options`; `complete` carries nothing.

expires_in.description: How long a challenge lives, in seconds. No handler of this fragment sets it, so the member is absent from every answer.

factors.description: The factors a second-factor step offers

fields.description: The inputs a challenge step asks for

kind.description: What the client does next: challenge, redirect, factor, enroll, complete or webauthn

kinds.description: The factor kinds an enroll step takes in

method.description: The HTTP method the redirect uses

options.description: The data a webauthn step carries: the public-key creation or request options of a WebAuthn ceremony, or, for a TOTP enrollment, an object with an `otpauth_uri` the client renders as a QR code.

provided_display_name.description: The provider's name for the person, carried by the pending signup of a social first login for the client to show read-only; absent when the provider gave none and for every other step

provided_email.description: The address the provider declared verified, carried by the pending signup of a social first login for the client to show read-only; absent when the provider declared no verified address and for every other step

provided_method.description: The stable name of the login method that started this flow, in the same vocabulary as methods[].name in the discovery document, such as github, google, wechat.mp or wechat.web; carried by the pending signup of a social first login so the client can name the provider; absent for every other step

resend_after.description: How soon a challenge may be asked for again, in seconds. No handler of this fragment sets it, so the member is absent from every answer.

url.description: Where a redirect step sends the user agent

AuthnLoginToken.description: The answer of a login completed with `delivery=token`, and of a token-delivered step-up: the state name, the token type, the access token, its lifetime and the refresh token.

access_token.description: The access token, sent in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <value>`.

expires_in.description: The access token's lifetime in seconds

refresh_token.description: Empty on a step-up, which issues no refresh token

state.description: authenticated for a login; elevated for a step-up, which issues no refresh token and carries it empty

token_type.description: The authorization scheme the access token is sent with; it is always `Bearer`.

AuthnMethodDescriptor.description: One login method as the discovery document reports it: its stable name, how a client renders it, the protocol a redirect or enterprise method speaks, its brand label, whether it can open an account, the provider values its bindings appear under, and the inputs its first step asks for.

binding_providers.description: The stored provider values, or namespace prefixes, the method's bindings appear under; absent means the method's name

fields.description: The inputs the method's first step asks for, empty for a method that does not open with a form

kind.description: How a client renders the method: form, redirect, enterprise or webauthn

label.description: The method's brand name where it has one, otherwise empty for a name-keyed translation

opens_account.description: Whether the method may open an account for an identifier it does not yet know; false for the phone and social methods when `authn.account.signup` is closed

protocol.description: The wire protocol a redirect or enterprise method speaks: oauth2, oidc or saml; empty otherwise

AuthnMfaFactor.description: One factor row of the caller's account: what the register holds about the factor, with nothing a kind keeps for itself.

activated_at.description: When the factor became active, as an RFC 3339 instant; absent until it is

created_at.description: When the factor row was created, as an RFC 3339 instant

id.description: The factor's identifier; use it as the `id` path parameter of `DELETE /auth/factors/{id}` or `PATCH /auth/factors/{id}`.

kind.description: The factor kind: `totp`, `sms` or `webauthn`.

label.description: The display label stored with the factor: what the caller submitted at registration or at a later rename, with surrounding whitespace trimmed. Empty means the factor has no name; the module generates none.

last_used_at.description: When the factor last passed a verification, as an RFC 3339 instant; absent until it first does

status.description: Lifecycle status: `pending` is registered but not yet confirmed and is never used to verify, `active` may verify, and `disabled` (left by an administrator reset or a clone warning) stays as a row that no longer counts.

AuthnMfaFactorList.description: An object whose single member lists every factor the caller's account has registered.

factors.description: The caller's factor rows, ordered oldest first by creation time and then by identifier; an empty array when the account has registered none.

AuthnProfileIdentifier.description: One identifier bound to the account, with the way its ownership was established.

contact.description: Whether the identifier is a contact of the account. A username never is; an email or phone is one the account selected, and an email written under the old behaviour is one

default_contact.description: Whether this proved email address is the one notifications to the account go to; at most one identifier of an account carries it

id.description: The identifier's own identifier

kind.description: The identifier kind: username, email or phone

proven.description: Whether the way of verification proves ownership: true for sms-code, email-code, invite and idp:<provider>, false for admin, import-unverified and self

sign_in.description: Whether the identifier is one the account signs in with. A username always is; an email or phone is only after it was proved and selected, and an identifier written under the old behaviour carries what that behaviour used

value.description: The identifier's value in the normalized form the account module stores: a username lower-cased, an email address trimmed and lower-cased, a phone number in E.164 with a leading plus sign and 7 to 15 digits

verified_at.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, the instant the identifier's ownership was established; always present, as no identifier is stored awaiting verification

verified_via.description: How the identifier's ownership was established: sms-code, email-code, invite, idp:<provider> (followed by the provider's identifier), admin, import-unverified or self. The first four prove ownership; admin, import-unverified and self only record a fact an administrator, an import or the account's own holder asserted

AuthnProfileLink.description: One external identity bound to the account, as the account module keeps it; it carries no provider subject.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, empty when the binding carries no creation instant

email.description: Absent when the provider gave no address

id.description: The binding's own identifier

last_login_at.description: Absent when the binding has never been used to sign in

provider.description: The provider the binding was made through, as the provider is registered

AuthnProfilePatch.description: The self-writable fields as they stand after a profile write, read back from what was stored.

attributes.description: The whole attribute set as it stands, never null

color_mode.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

display_name.description: The display name as it stands after the write; the account's current one when the body carried none

locale.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

time_zone.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

AuthnProfileProfile.description: The caller's own profile: the account's self fields plus its identifiers and external bindings, which this surface only reads. It is built field by field from the account module's values, so a field added to the record there does not reach a client by being there.

account_id.description: The account's identifier, the one the request's identity names; never empty on a 200.

attributes.description: Never null; the empty object when the account carries none

color_mode.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

created_at.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, empty when the account carries no creation instant

display_name.description: The account's display name, empty when it carries none

identifiers.description: The account's identifiers; always an array, never null, and empty when the account has none. An email the account holds is among them even while it is unproved; a pending reservation is not an identifier and is not listed

kind.description: The account's kind: user or service, a service being a non-interactive API client.

links.description: The account's external bindings; always an array, never null, and empty when there are none. The provider's own subject for the person is not included

locale.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

mfa_required.description: Whether the account must register a factor

password_set.description: Whether the account has a password credential set

time_zone.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

verification.description: How far the account's email verification has got, read at request time and never stored in a session or an access token

AuthnProfileVerification.description: How far the account's email verification has got, read on this request: none when it has no email address to verify, pending when it holds an address that has not been proved, verified when it holds one whose ownership was proved.

email.description: The address of the state: for verified the proved address verified earliest, ties broken by identifier; for pending the earliest unproved address or reservation awaiting verification, ties broken by identifier; empty for none

since.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, the first instant the account reached verified; empty while it never did, and for none

state.description: none, pending or verified. none means the account has no email address to verify; pending means it has an email address that has not been proved, whether the account itself, an administrator or an import wrote it; verified means an email address whose ownership was proved

AuthnSessionItem.description: One live session of the caller's, as the listing reports it.

client_ip.description: Empty when the session carries none

created_at.description: When the session was created, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

current.description: Whether this is the session the request came with

expires_at.description: The absolute expiry, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC. A browser session can stop being valid earlier, once its idle timeout passes.

id.description: The public session identifier; it names the row and is not a credential.

kind.description: The session kind, browser or token; service-account sessions are never listed.

last_seen_at.description: Last activity of the session, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC. For a browser session this is the last use the row was written for: touches are coalesced, written at most once per effective touch interval — the configured interval capped at half the idle timeout — so the value lags the newest use by up to that interval. A token session has no renewal path, so its value is the creation time.

user_agent.description: Empty when the session carries none

AuthnSessionList.description: The caller's own live sessions, in the order the listing reports them.

sessions.description: The live browser and token sessions of the account, most recently created first; the empty array when there are none.

AuthnSessionRevoked.description: The outcome of revoking every session of the caller's but the current one.

AuthnSessionView.description: Whether the request carries a signed-in identity and, when it does, the facts the identity is built from.

account_id.description: The account the request is taken to be from; the impersonated account while impersonating

actor_id.description: The account whose hands are on the request; present only while impersonating

assurance.description: The assurance level the authentication reached; "none" when the identity carries no level.

auth_time.description: The instant of the last interactive authentication, absent when the identity carries none

authenticated.description: False when nobody is signed in; every other field is then absent

impersonating.description: True only while the identity is impersonating another account; absent otherwise.

methods.description: The authentication methods the identity completed, each from the closed set named by the enum; absent when the session records none.

provider.description: The backend that verified the credential

session_id.description: The public identifier of the session the request came with; absent when nobody is signed in.

AuthnSsoProvider.description: One SSO sign-in entry a client can offer for a domain. It carries only public identity; no endpoint, configuration or secret is exposed.

id.description: The provider's opaque identifier, used to start a sign-in flow for this provider.

name.description: The tenant-chosen display name of the provider, meant to be shown on the sign-in screen.

protocol.description: The protocol the provider's sign-in entry uses

AuthnTokenJWK.description: One public JSON Web Key. The published keys carry `kty`, `kid`, `alg` and `use`; the remaining members depend on the key type: an EC key carries `crv`, `x` and `y`, an RSA key carries `n` and `e`.

alg.description: The signature algorithm the key signs and verifies with

crv.description: The curve of an EC key; only P-256 is supported, so this is `P-256`.

e.description: The public exponent of an RSA public key, base64url-encoded without padding.

kid.description: The RFC 7638 thumbprint of the public key

kty.description: The key type, for example EC or RSA

n.description: The modulus of an RSA public key, at least 2048 bits, base64url-encoded without padding.

x.description: The x coordinate of an EC public key, base64url-encoded without padding.

y.description: The y coordinate of an EC public key, base64url-encoded without padding.

AuthnTokenJWKS.description: The public key set published on `GET /auth/jwks.json`, served as `application/jwk-set+json`. It holds the public half of every key loaded at startup and no private field.

keys.description: Every configured key's public JWK; the set is never empty.

AuthnTokenOAuthError.description: The failure body of RFC 6749 §5.2, which the token and revocation endpoints answer in place of the entry point's problem+json. Its only member is `error`; no `error_description` accompanies it.

error.description: The machine-readable failure code, one of `invalid_request`, `invalid_client`, `invalid_grant`, `unsupported_grant_type` and `temporarily_unavailable`.

AuthnTokenResponse.description: The success body of `POST /auth/token`, per RFC 6749 §5.1. A `client_credentials` response carries no `refresh_token`.

access_token.description: The signed access token: a compact JWT, presented as a `Bearer` credential.

expires_in.description: The access token's remaining lifetime in whole seconds

refresh_token.description: Present only for the refresh_token grant

AuthzAdminBindingView.description: One role binding: an account holds a role within a tenant.

account.description: The account the role is bound to.

granted_at.description: When the binding was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

role.description: The role bound to the account.

tenant.description: The tenant the binding belongs to.

AuthzAdminGrantView.description: One permission grant of a role: the permission it was written as, and the (resource, action) pair the policy engine matches on.

action.description: The action the grant matches on, kept beside the permission so an untranslatable grant can still be diagnosed.

created_at.description: When the grant was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

permission.description: The permission the (resource, action) pair translates to, for example authz.role.manage; the empty string when the pair matches no declared permission, which is a grant left from a vocabulary this process no longer carries.

resource.description: The resource the grant matches on, kept beside the permission so an untranslatable grant can still be diagnosed.

tenant.description: The tenant the grant belongs to.

dangerous.description: True when granting the permission widens the grantee's power over other accounts or over the tenant's policy; a client calls such a permission out before an operator grants it, and asks for a deliberate second confirmation.

description.description: The permission's description, rendered in the request's language from the key the declaring module gave it. Empty when the assembly delivers no message localizer or the module gave the permission no description key. A key no catalog carries comes back as the key itself, the i18n fallback; a client shows the text as received and does not resolve keys.

grantable.description: True when the caller holds the permission in the platform domain and may therefore grant it to a role. A permission the caller does not hold is still listed: the catalog is the whole declared set, not the caller's grantable subset.

group.description: The group the declaring module places the permission in, for example authorization or membership. Empty when the module gave it no group; a client groups such a permission as it sees fit.

permission.description: The permission name as the catalog declares it, for example authn.tenant.access. Only the authn.* permissions are the same vocabulary as authn.Action and carry its string; a permission outside it, such as authz.role.read, has no corresponding authn.Action.

AuthzAdminRoleView.description: One role of a tenant as the role routes report it.

builtin.description: True for a builtin role: the management face can neither rewrite nor remove it, nor change its grants. The mark is set by the host that seeds the policy data and is never cleared.

can_manage.description: True when the caller holds authz.role.manage in the platform domain, so a client renders the role, grant and binding controls. False hides them; the route guard still refuses a write the caller may not make.

created_at.description: When the role was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

description.description: The role's description as a client shows it: the operator's free text for a role this surface created, or a builtin role's description key rendered in the request's language. With no message localizer assembled, a builtin role answers its key itself, the i18n fallback.

member_count.description: How many active members hold the role. Null when the assembly delivers no account-identity reader: the count cannot be read, and the binding count is not a stand-in for it.

permission_count.description: How many permission grants the role holds, from one grouped read of the tenant's grants.

role.description: The role name within the tenant.

tenant.description: The tenant the role belongs to.

AuthzAdminRoleWrite.description: The body of a role write: the role's description. The builtin mark is not part of the body; a member sent under that name reaches nothing.

description.description: The role's free-text description, at most 500 characters. Absent leaves the stored text as it is; an explicit empty string clears it; an over-long value is a 400.

AuthzTenantAdminBindingView.description: One role binding: an account holds a role within a tenant.

account.description: The account the role is bound to.

granted_at.description: When the binding was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

role.description: The role bound to the account.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the binding belongs to.

AuthzTenantAdminGrantView.description: One permission grant of a role: the permission it was written as, and the (resource, action) pair the policy engine matches on.

action.description: The action the grant matches on, kept beside the permission so an untranslatable grant can still be diagnosed.

created_at.description: When the grant was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

permission.description: The permission the (resource, action) pair translates to, for example authz.tenant.role.manage; the empty string when the pair matches no declared permission, which is a grant left from a vocabulary this process no longer carries.

resource.description: The resource the grant matches on, kept beside the permission so an untranslatable grant can still be diagnosed.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the grant belongs to.

AuthzTenantAdminPermissionView.description: One permission of the tenant-governed set.

dangerous.description: True when granting the permission widens the grantee's power over other accounts or over the tenant's policy; a client calls such a permission out before an operator grants it.

description.description: The permission's description, rendered in the request's language from the key the declaring module gave it. Empty when the assembly delivers no message localizer or the module gave the permission no description key. A key no catalog carries comes back as the key itself, the i18n fallback.

grantable.description: True when the caller holds the permission in the tenant and may therefore grant it to a role. A permission the caller does not hold is still listed: the catalog is the whole governed set, not the caller's grantable subset.

group.description: The group the declaring module places the permission in, for example authorization or membership. Empty when the module gave it no group; a client groups such a permission as it sees fit.

permission.description: The permission name as the catalog declares it, for example authz.tenant.role.read. Only the authn.* permissions are the same vocabulary as authn.Action and carry its string.

AuthzTenantAdminRoleBindingView.description: One account holding a role within a tenant, as the role usage read shows it.

account.description: The account the role is bound to.

active.description: Whether the account is still active. Null when the assembly delivers no account identity reader or the reader does not know the account: an unavailable identity state is reported as unknown, never as false.

display_name.description: The account's display name, as the host's account identity reader reports it. Empty when the assembly delivers no identity reader or the reader knows no name for the account.

granted_at.description: When the binding was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

username.description: The account's login username, as the host's account identity reader reports it: unique, user-facing, and not an identifier of the account. Empty when the assembly delivers no identity reader or the account has none; it is never a fallback to another login identifier.

AuthzTenantAdminRoleView.description: One role of a tenant as the role routes report it.

builtin.description: True for a builtin role: the tenant management face can neither rewrite nor remove it, nor change its grants. The mark is set by the host that seeds the policy data and is never cleared.

can_manage.description: True when the caller holds authz.tenant.role.manage in the tenant, which decides whether a client renders the grant and revoke controls.

created_at.description: When the role was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

description.description: The role's description in the request's language: a builtin role's key is rendered through the message localizer (falling back to the key), and a role the management face created carries the operator's free text as written.

member_count.description: How many active members hold the role within the tenant. Null when the assembly delivers no account identity reader: the count cannot be told apart from an unavailable identity state, so it is not reported as zero.

permission_count.description: How many permission grants the role holds within the tenant. A role holding none answers zero.

role.description: The role name within the tenant. A role is never renamed: the name is the key a binding holds.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the role belongs to.

AuthzTenantAdminRoleWrite.description: The body of a role write: the role's description. The builtin mark and the role name are not part of the body; a member sent under those names reaches nothing.

description.description: The role's free-text description, at most 500 characters. Absent leaves the stored text as it is; an explicit empty string clears it; an over-long value is a 400.

CaptchaChallengeResponse.description: A captcha challenge: its id, the form it takes, the instruction key a client words for that form, the media paths the form carries and how long it stays valid.

audio_url.description: The path of the spoken digits of an audio challenge.

background_url.description: The path of the background of a slider challenge.

expires_in.description: How long the challenge stays valid, in whole seconds. A proof that names an expired challenge is refused.

form.description: The challenge form: image for a picture of digits, slider for a background and a piece to slide over it, audio for a spoken reading of digits.

id.description: The challenge id a proof names, base64url without padding.

image_url.description: The path of the digit picture of an image challenge.

instruction.description: A stable key naming the instruction a client shows for the form. The text itself is the client's language resource.

piece_url.description: The path of the piece a slider challenge slides over its background.

provider.description: The mechanism that issued the challenge: the constant captcha.

ChallengeResponse.description: A proof-of-work challenge, the work it takes to solve, and how long it stays valid.

algorithm.description: The hash a proof is computed with: sha256.

challenge.description: The random challenge, base64url without padding. Solve it into a nonce, and present the two joined by a dot as the proof.

difficulty.description: The number of leading zero bits the proof's hash must carry; higher values take exponentially more work.

expires_in.description: How long the challenge stays valid, in whole seconds. A proof that names an expired challenge is refused.

provider.description: The mechanism that issued the challenge: the constant pow.

Channel.description: A delivery channel the capability carries: in_app writes a row the inbox reads, email goes through the mail capability's sender, and sms goes through the SMS registry's sender. The set is closed.

FeatureBoardDocument.description: The feature document: the feature names this process serves, decided by the assembly at start and frozen before the first request, so it is the same for every caller and every tenant. The object is extensible — a field added beside features is a compatible change — and carries no feature of its own.

features.description: The feature names this process serves, ascending and without repetition. Each name answers whether a frontend surface the caller's build carries is served here; the response carries no configuration value, method descriptor or rendering description.

MyTransferView.description: One owner-transfer request addressed to the caller.

expiresAt.description: When the confirmation window closes, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

id.description: The request identifier.

requestedAt.description: When the request was made, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

status.description: The request's state. Only pending requests can be confirmed or declined.

tenant.description: The organization whose ownership the request is about, by its name.

NotificationMessage.description: One in-app message as the inbox shows it. The title and body arrive already rendered, and the bookkeeping columns — tenant, recipient, dedupe key, expiry and update time — are not part of this view.

body.description: The rendered body, in the language the delivery pipeline rendered it in.

created_at.description: When the message was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

group.description: The group the message was filed under; the listing filters on it. Empty when the message was filed under none.

id.description: The message identifier; it is the value the per-message mark-read route takes.

link.description: The optional navigation target; the empty string when the message carries none.

params.description: The type's parameters after the allow-list filter, as an opaque JSON object the client renders into the message; null when the message carries none.

read_at.description: The first-read instant as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC; null while the message is unread, and never rewritten once set.

title.description: The rendered title, in the language the delivery pipeline rendered it in.

type_key.description: The notification type key the message was dispatched under, shaped like <module>.<entity>.<action>.

NotificationPreference.description: One row of the caller's preference matrix: a notification type and the channels that type's dispatches would go out under for the caller.

channels.description: The caller's effective channel set for the type: the stored channels when a row exists, otherwise the type's default channels; a type that cannot be unsubscribed always carries its default channels.

explicit.description: True when the channels came from a stored row, false when they are the type's default channels

group.description: The type's grouping label, copied from its declaration.

type_key.description: The notification type key this row describes.

NotificationSetPreferenceRequest.description: The body of a single-channel preference update.

enabled.description: The target state of the channel; a body naming none is told apart from one naming false

NotificationType.description: One notification type as declared by the business module that owns it; the taxonomy is fixed at startup and read-only for the life of the process.

default_channels.description: The channels a recipient gets for this type when no preference row is stored. Non-empty, free of duplicates, and drawn from the channel set.

group.description: The grouping label the declaring module assigns to the type.

key.description: The globally unique type key; two modules declaring one key fail the process startup.

recipient_visible_params.description: The parameter names the declaring module allows to be shown to the recipient. This module stores and returns the list but does not interpret it.

unsubscribable.description: Whether a recipient may change this type's channel set. False means writes answer 409 and the effective set is always default_channels.

OpsDocument.description: The merged OpenAPI document: the version it declares, its info section, every merged path, the components its fragments declared, and x-fragments naming each source

OpsHealth.description: The liveness response body: a single status field, always ok on a process that can answer.

status.description: The literal the liveness route writes; a live process always answers ok

OpsReadiness.description: The readiness response body, carrying the verdict and, when it is unavailable, one line per part that failed.

failures.description: One line per part that failed; absent when the verdict is ready

status.description: ready when every part answered, unavailable otherwise

OrganizationCreateRequest.description: The name, display name and description of the organization to create. The identifier is generated.

description.description: The organization's description; at most 500 runes after trimming.

display_name.description: The organization's display name; 1 to 100 runes after trimming, and the surface requires it non-empty.

name.description: The organization's public name: a lower-case slug of 3 to 63 letters, digits and dashes, beginning with a letter or a digit. It is unique across the roster and cannot be changed after creation.

OrganizationCreatedTenant.description: The created organization: the caller's name and profile, and the active state. The generated identifier is internal and never appears.

name.description: The request-surface name the caller chose; unique across the roster and immutable after creation.

status.description: The organization's state; a self-service organization starts active.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

SettingsAdminSetting.description: One declared setting item as this management surface shows it, on the selected layer. The declaration fields come from the key table; written, has_row and value come from that layer's rows and from the resolved read. Every value-bearing field is text in the declared type's own form, so a duration reads as "5m0s" rather than as a count of nanoseconds.

default.description: The declared default in the declared type's text form, empty for a sensitive item

description.description: The human-readable text the declaring module gave the item.

domain.description: The declared rule over the item's values, empty when every value of the type is admitted

has_row.description: Whether the selected layer holds a row for the item. For a non-sensitive item, written is empty both when no row is held and when the row's text is empty; a sensitive item's written is the mask string whether or not a row exists.

key.description: The full setting key: the declaring module's namespace joined with the item's own segment by a dot.

namespace.description: The module that declared the item

sensitive.description: Whether the item is a credential. A sensitive item's default is empty and its written and value carry a fixed mask string; has_row still reports whether the layer holds a row.

type.description: The declared type's name as reflection reports it, such as "string", "int", "bool" or "time.Duration"; the item's values are stored and rendered in that type's text form.

value.description: The text the item resolves to after the three-level fallback, the mask string for a sensitive item

written.description: The text the selected layer holds, the mask string for a sensitive item

SettingsTenantAdminSetting.description: One declared setting item as the tenant management surface shows it. The declaration fields and the item's control metadata come from the key table; the three value fields come from the tenant layer's rows and the global layer's rows, and every value-bearing field is text in the declared type's own form.

control.description: The control the surface renders for the item.

danger.description: How destructive turning the item off is: "critical" when the surface must confirm the change first, empty when there is no such warning.

description.description: The item's description, rendered in the request's language from the declaration's key, falling back to the declared English text when no localizer is assembled.

effect.description: When a change to the item takes effect: "immediate" when it applies as soon as it is saved, "next-sign-in" when it applies to a member at the next sign-in, empty when the declaration names none.

effective_value.description: The text the item resolves to: the platform policy OR the tenant policy, in the declared type's text form. The mask string for a sensitive item.

has_row.description: Whether the tenant layer holds an explicit row for the item, whether or not the platform policy is forcing the effective value.

key.description: The full setting key: the declaring module's namespace joined with the item's own segment by a dot.

locked_by_platform.description: Whether the platform layer holds this policy on, so that a tenant write turning it off answers 409 tenant-admission-enforced.

platform_value.description: The global layer's value in the declared type's text form, the declared default when the global layer holds no row. The mask string for a sensitive item.

source.description: The layer the effective value comes from: "global" when the platform policy is on or the global layer holds a row, "tenant" when the tenant holds a row and the platform is not forcing the item, "default" when neither holds a row.

tenant_access.description: How much of the item the tenant surface exposes: "read" for a visible but unwritable item, "read-write" for one the tenant may change.

tenant_value.description: The tenant layer's value in the declared type's text form, the declared default when the tenant holds no row. The mask string for a sensitive item.

title.description: The item's title, rendered in the request's language from the declaration's key, falling back to the declared English text when no localizer is assembled.

type.description: The declared type's name as reflection reports it. The tenant surface renders switches, so this is "bool".

SettingsTenantAdminSettings.description: The tenant settings surface's read answer: the declared items it exposes and whether the tenant's settings may be written at all.

read_only_reason.description: Why the surface is read-only, empty when writable is true. The closed set is the refusal code this capability writes for the same condition: "protected" when the host's settings write seam refuses the tenant, "unavailable" when the seam cannot answer. The listing still answers 200 with the settings it read in both cases.

settings.description: The items whose declarations expose them to a tenant, each with its platform value, tenant value and effective value.

writable.description: Whether this tenant's settings may be written through this surface. False when the host's settings write seam refuses the tenant, in which case every write route answers 403 protected, and when the seam cannot answer, in which case every write route answers 503.

SmsAdminApproval.description: The vendor's review verdict on one template in one language.

reason.description: The vendor's own explanation, present when it turned the template down and it gave one; omitted otherwise.

state.description: The verdict in this capability's own vocabulary: pending, approved, rejected, withdrawn or not-required; an empty string means a review this process does not track. Not-required means the mounted carrier has no per-template review, which is not the same as a review this process does not follow. The vendor's raw status numbers are never exposed.

SmsAdminCarrier.description: The mounted carrier's declaration of what it can carry.

async_receipt.description: Whether the vendor's final delivery state arrives asynchronously: a synchronous answer carries only the vendor's message identifier, and acceptance is not delivery.

attribute_keys.description: The template attribute keys this carrier accepts: the vendor registration identifiers a template may carry. An attribute under any other key is refused at declaration, load or write.

content.description: Which template shape the carrier sends under: the vendor's template code, the body the declaration rendered, or both.

countries.description: The countries this carrier can reach. Empty means it declares no restriction of its own.

identities.description: The sending identities this deployment has, each with the countries it can serve. Empty for a carrier that sends from one fixed account.

max_body_runes.description: The bound on a rendered body, in runes. Zero means the capability sets no bound of its own.

name.description: The carrier this process mounted; one process sends through exactly one carrier.

review.description: How the vendor reviews a template, and whether a send may pick its identity.

SmsAdminContentSupport.description: Which template shape a carrier sends under.

template_code.description: Whether the carrier sends by the vendor's template code.

text_body.description: Whether the carrier sends the body the declaration rendered.

SmsAdminIdentity.description: One sending identity this deployment has, and the countries it can serve.

attributes.description: Vendor-specific values the identity needs, such as a sender address that lives beside a messaging service. Empty when it needs none.

countries.description: The countries it can serve. Empty means it serves every country the carrier reaches.

kind.description: What sort of identity it is: sign-name, sender-id, long-code, short-code, toll-free, pool or messaging-service.

name.description: What a message names the identity by.

value.description: The vendor's own value for it: a signature, a number, a service identifier.

SmsAdminRegister.description: A template to take up by the vendor code the deployment already holds: its name, what it is for, its parameters, the vendor code and the body of each language, and its registration identifiers.

attributes.description: The vendor registration identifiers the template carries, keyed by the keys the mounted carrier accepts. Optional.

bodies.description: The locally rendered body per language, keyed by locale. Optional; every language named needs a non-empty body whose ${name} placeholders all name declared parameters, and each language needs a code, a body, or both.

codes.description: The vendor's template code per language, keyed by locale. Optional; every language named needs a non-empty code, and each language needs a code, a body, or both.

kind.description: What the template is for: verification, notification or marketing. Optional; an unset value means notification.

name.description: The logical template name to take up; required and non-empty, and the name a caller will later send under. A language the name already holds is a 409.

params.description: The parameter names the template substitutes, in the order the vendor approved them. May be empty.

SmsAdminReviewSupport.description: How a vendor reviews a template and whether a send may pick its identity.

originator.description: Whether a send may name the identity it goes out from. False means the carrier has one fixed sending identity.

per_template.description: Whether the vendor reviews each template, so a template is only sendable once the review has come back approved. False means there is no such review and every language starts not-required.

SmsAdminSubmission.description: A template submission to the vendor for one language: the body with its placeholders, what the template is for, and the note its reviewer reads.

attributes.description: The vendor registration identifiers the template carries, keyed by the keys the mounted carrier accepts. Optional.

content.description: The template body, written with ${name} placeholders naming the entries of params. The carrier rewrites them into the vendor's own syntax, in params order.

kind.description: What the template is for, in the shared vocabulary: verification, notification or marketing. The carrier maps it to the vendor's spelling.

locale.description: The language this submission is for, opaque to the capability. A vendor approves per language, so one submission yields one code for one language.

name.description: The logical template name the submission creates; required and non-empty.

params.description: The parameter names content substitutes, in the order the template expects them. May be empty.

remark.description: A note for the vendor's reviewer; may be empty.

SmsAdminTemplate.description: One template as the management surface reports it: its logical name, its carrier, what it is for, its source, its ordered parameter names, the languages it holds a code or a body for, its bodies and registration identifiers, the vendor's review per language, whether sends are allowed, and its write counters. It carries no vendor code.

approvals.description: The vendor's review verdict per language, keyed by locale. A carrier that reviews each template approves per language; one with no such review answers not-required per language. A configured template carries an empty object because this process does not track its review.

attributes.description: The vendor registration identifiers the template carries, keyed by the keys the mounted carrier accepts. Empty when it carries none.

bodies.description: The locally rendered bodies, keyed by locale. A template that sends only by vendor code carries an empty object.

carrier.description: The carrier this template belongs to. A database serves one carrier, and every record in it names that one.

created_at.description: When the record was first written, in UTC and RFC 3339 format; the zero time for a configured template.

enabled.description: Whether a message may go out under the template. A configured template is always enabled; a runtime template's value is set by the enable route and is independent of the vendor's review.

kind.description: What the template is for: verification, notification or marketing. A template that named none when it was declared is a notification.

locales.description: The effective language set: the languages the template holds a vendor code for, a body for, or both. Whether a language can be sent in follows the mounted carrier's declared review: a carrier that reviews each template sends only while the vendor's review for that language is approved, while a carrier with no per-template review holds every language it has a code or a body for as sendable. A configured template's review is not tracked, so each language it holds can be sent in.

name.description: The logical template name a caller sends under; the management routes address a template by it.

params.description: The parameter names the template substitutes, in the order the vendor approved them; a positional vendor lays values out in this order. May be empty.

source.description: Where the template came from: config for one read from the configuration, runtime for one this process created. A config template is read-only at runtime, always enabled, and carries no approvals and no version.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written, in UTC and RFC 3339 format; the zero time for a configured template.

version.description: The number of writes this runtime record has taken, used as the optimistic-concurrency condition; 0 for a configured template, which has no version.

TenantAdminTenant.description: One tenant as the management routes render it: the name, the kind, the organization profile, the owner account, the state, the creation time and who disabled it while it is disabled.

contactEmail.description: The organization's contact address. Empty when its profile names none. It is the organization's address, not a login identity.

createdAt.description: When the tenant was registered, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

description.description: The organization's description. Empty when its profile names none.

disabledBy.description: Who disabled the tenant: operator through a status change, or account through the account's own state. Present only while the state is disabled.

displayName.description: The organization's display name. Empty when its profile names none; a surface falls back to the name then.

kind.description: The tenant's kind: business for an ordinary tenant, personal for the single-person space a host derives for an account. A client branches on this value, never on the name.

name.description: The name the request surface addresses the tenant by, and the one every view and path uses.

ownerAccount.description: The account that owns the organization, from the roster row's owner column. Empty for a tenant that carries no owner, such as the platform's own tenant. This is a platform-domain detail; no member-facing view carries it.

status.description: The tenant's state: active is served, disabled is not and may be served again, deleted is a tombstone that is never served again.

website.description: The organization's absolute http or https address. Empty when its profile names none.

account.description: The account identifier of the active member the request names as the next owner.

contact_email.description: The organization's contact address, one bare email address of at most 254 bytes. Empty clears it.

description.description: A longer account of the organization, at most 500 runes. Empty clears it.

display_name.description: The organization's display name, at most 100 runes. Empty clears it; a surface then falls back to the name.

website.description: The organization's absolute http or https address, at most 2048 bytes, with a host and no userinfo. Empty clears it.

TenantAdminTenantRegistration.description: The name and optional profile of a tenant to register. The identifier is generated and the state starts active, so neither is part of the body.

contact_email.description: The organization's contact address, one bare email address of at most 254 bytes.

description.description: A longer account of the organization, at most 500 runes.

display_name.description: The organization's display name, at most 100 runes. Empty when the registration names none.

name.description: The name to give the tenant; the roster refuses one another tenant already holds.

website.description: The organization's absolute http or https address, at most 2048 bytes, with a host and no userinfo.

account.description: The account identifier of the active member the request names as the next owner.

TenantProfileView.description: One tenant's organization profile: the read-only name, the kind, the owner shown by display name and username, the state and the four descriptive fields, behind tenant.profile.read.

contactEmail.description: The organization's contact address. Empty when its profile names none. It is the organization's address, not a login identity.

createdAt.description: When the tenant was registered, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

description.description: The organization's description. Empty when its profile names none.

displayName.description: The organization's display name. Empty when its profile names none; a surface falls back to the name then.

kind.description: The tenant's kind: business for an ordinary tenant, personal for the single-person space a host derives for an account. A client branches on this value, never on the name.

name.description: The name the request surface addresses the tenant by.

ownerAccount.description: The owning account's internal identifier, from the roster row's owner column. It is the key the ownership decision and the transfer-target exclusion use, and a client compares it to identify the owner; it is not displayed. A business organization carries one; a personal organization's owner is the account itself. Empty only for a tenant the roster holds with no owner.

ownerDisplayName.description: The owner's display name, read from the account store. It is not the account identifier. Empty when the owner cannot be resolved, and never an identifier.

ownerUsername.description: The owner's account username, read from the account store: unique and user-facing, and not the account identifier. Empty when the owner cannot be resolved or the account has none, and never an identifier.

status.description: The tenant's state: active is served, disabled is not and may be served again, deleted is a tombstone that is never served again.

website.description: The organization's absolute http or https address. Empty when its profile names none.

contact_email.description: The organization's contact address, one bare email address of at most 254 bytes. Empty clears it.

description.description: A longer account of the organization, at most 500 runes. Empty clears it.

display_name.description: The organization's display name, at most 100 runes. Empty clears it; a surface then falls back to the name.

website.description: The organization's absolute http or https address, at most 2048 bytes, with a host and no userinfo. Empty clears it.

TenantTransferView.description: One pending or finished owner-transfer request on the organization's own surface.

expiresAt.description: When the confirmation window closes, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

id.description: The request identifier the target and the canonical paths address.

requestedAt.description: When the request was made, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

status.description: The request's state. Only pending requests can be cancelled or confirmed.

targetDisplayName.description: The target account's display name. Empty when the account store does not resolve it.

targetUsername.description: The target account's username. Empty when the account store does not resolve it.

bearerAuth.description: A credential in the Authorization header, written by the caller. The gateway reads the scheme and hands the credential to the backend that declares it.

sessionCookie.description: The session cookie a browser attaches by itself. It is __Host-sid, or __Secure-sid when the deployment configures a cookie domain.
sessionCookie.name: __Host-sid
